stem: What problem does service discovery solve for Prometheus?

options.text: Keeping the list of scrape targets current as instances come and go
options.note: Right. SD asks an authoritative system for the current targets, so you don't hard-code them.
Compression is a storage concern, unrelated to SD.

options.text: Routing alerts to the right team
options.note: That's Alertmanager's routing, not service discovery.
Service discovery finds targets. It doesn't process logs.

explanation: Targets may be configured statically via static_configs or discovered dynamically using one of the supported service discovery mechanisms.
hint: Think about a cluster where pods are rescheduled all the time.

stem: You add a new target to a file used by file_sd_configs. What do you need to do for Prometheus to pick it up?

options.text: Nothing. File changes are detected through disk watches and applied immediately
options.note: Right. File SD watches its files, so no restart or reload is needed.
Not needed. File SD detects changes on its own.

options.text: Send SIGHUP to reload the configuration
options.note: That's for changes to prometheus.yml itself. File SD target files are watched.
evaluation_interval is for rule evaluation, not target discovery.

explanation: File-based SD reads files containing static configs. Changes to all defined files are detected via disk watches and applied immediately, with a periodic re-read as a fallback.
hint: File SD is designed so other tools can update targets without touching Prometheus.

stem: Your company uses an in-house service registry that Prometheus doesn't support. What does the documentation suggest?

options.text: Write the registry's targets to files and use file-based service discovery
options.note: Right. File SD is the docs' suggested interface for unsupported discovery systems (HTTP SD is a related option).

options.text: Fork Prometheus and add the registry to its source code
options.note: Possible in theory, but the docs point to file SD as the generic interface.

options.text: Make each service push to the Pushgateway
options.note: That swaps discovery for pushing and brings the Pushgateway's pitfalls.

options.text: Add the registry lookup inside each exporter
options.note: The docs say service discovery should be done in Prometheus, not in exporters.

explanation: File-based SD provides a generic way to configure static targets and serves as an interface to plug in custom service discovery mechanisms.
hint: Which SD mechanism is described as a generic interface?

stem: Which file formats does file-based service discovery accept? Select all that apply.

options.note: Right. Files may be YAML.
Right. Files may be JSON.
CSV isn't supported. Use YAML or JSON lists of static configs.
That format is for metrics, not target lists.

explanation: File SD files may be provided in YAML or JSON format, containing a list of static configs.

stem: Kubernetes SD gives each target a __meta_kubernetes_namespace label. You don't add any relabel rules. Will stored series carry this label?

options.text: No. Labels starting with __ are dropped after relabeling, so you must copy it into a normal label
options.note: Right. __meta labels are only available during the relabeling phase.

options.text: Yes, all SD metadata is stored with every series
options.note: Metadata labels start with __ and are removed after relabeling.

options.text: Yes, but only for pod-role targets
options.note: The rule is the same for every role: __ labels are dropped.
honor_labels deals with conflicts between scraped and server labels, not with __meta labels.

explanation: SD mechanisms add labels prefixed with __meta_ during relabeling. Labels starting with __ are removed after target relabeling, so you copy what you need into regular labels.
hint: Remember what happens to double-underscore labels.

stem: Which relabel rule copies the discovered Kubernetes namespace into a namespace label on every scraped series?

options.note: Right. replace with the default regex (.*) copies the whole value into target_label.
That copies in the wrong direction, into a label that gets dropped anyway.
labeldrop removes labels. It doesn't copy them.
drop removes whole targets that match. It doesn't copy anything.

explanation: replace (the default action) matches regex (default (.*)) against the source labels and writes the replacement (default $1) into target_label.
hint: Source is the meta label; target is the label you want to keep.

stem: Which of these are valid role values for kubernetes_sd_configs? Select all that apply.

options.note: Right. Discovers pods and exposes their container ports as targets.
Right. One target per cluster node.
Right. One target per service port, often for blackbox probing.
There's no deployment role. The roles are node, service, pod, endpoints, endpointslice and ingress.

explanation: Kubernetes SD roles: node, service, pod, endpoints, endpointslice and ingress.
hint: One of these is a Kubernetes object that isn't directly scrapeable.

stem: How does Kubernetes service discovery get its targets?

options.text: By retrieving them from the Kubernetes REST API and staying synchronised with cluster state
options.note: Right. That's how the docs describe it.

options.text: By reading a file the cluster writes every 5 minutes
options.note: That would be file SD. Kubernetes SD talks to the API directly.

options.text: By scanning every IP in the cluster network
options.note: There's no network scanning. It uses the API.

options.text: By having each pod push its address to Prometheus
options.note: Prometheus pulls the information from the Kubernetes API.

explanation: Kubernetes SD configurations allow retrieving scrape targets from Kubernetes' REST API and always staying synchronised with the cluster state.
hint: Kubernetes has an API that knows about every object.

stem: How does HTTP SD differ from file SD?

options.text: HTTP SD polls an endpoint on a refresh interval; file SD is event-based and updates instantly via file watches
options.note: Right. That's the comparison table in the HTTP SD docs.

options.text: HTTP SD supports YAML while file SD supports only JSON
options.note: Reversed. File SD accepts YAML or JSON, while HTTP SD uses JSON.

options.text: HTTP SD requires restarting Prometheus to see changes
options.note: Neither needs a restart. HTTP SD refreshes on its interval.

options.text: File SD supports TLS and OAuth2
options.note: Those security options apply to HTTP SD's transport. File SD relies on file permissions.

explanation: From the comparison table: file SD is event-based (inotify) with instant updates and YAML/JSON. HTTP SD follows refresh_interval, uses JSON over HTTP(S), and supports TLS, basic auth and OAuth2.
hint: One reacts to events; the other checks on a timer.

stem: Where should service discovery logic live, according to the exporter-writing guide?

options.note: Right. Exporters stay simple, and Prometheus discovers the targets.
The guide says the opposite.
Alertmanager handles alerts, not targets.
Grafana visualises data. It doesn't discover scrape targets.

explanation: The deployment section of the exporter-writing guide states that all service discovery is done in Prometheus, not in exporters.

stem: Which DNS record types can dns_sd_configs query? Select all that apply.

options.note: Right. SRV records carry both host and port.
Right. Basic A records are supported.
Right. IPv6 AAAA records are supported.
TXT isn't in the supported list (A, AAAA, MX, NS, SRV).

explanation: DNS SD supports basic DNS A, AAAA, MX, NS and SRV record queries, but not the advanced DNS-SD approach in RFC 6763.
hint: Think of records that point at hosts (and ports).
